deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler, Tractatus de numerorum doctrina (E792), Cap. 10, on quadratic residues modulo an odd prime d = 2p+1. In §§309-313 (previous page) he defined the complement d-r of a residue r. He showed that either every residue has its complement among the residues or none does, depending on whether -1 is a residue. Since complements pair up distinct residues and the number of residues is p, the case 'all complements are residues' requires p to be even.

§314 (continued from p.38). Let p = 2q-1 be odd, so the prime is d = 4q-1. Then for every residue α, the complement 4q-1-α ≡ -α is a non-residue. Equivalently, no square leaves remainder 4q-1-α when divided by 4q-1.

§315. Take α = n². Then no square m² satisfies m² ≡ 4q-1-n² (mod 4q-1), i.e. m² + n² ≢ 0 (mod 4q-1).
- Implicit step (mine): this needs n² to be a nonzero residue, i.e. 4q-1 ∤ n.
- If 4q-1 | n, then m² + n² ≡ 0 forces 4q-1 | m.
- Hence a prime 4q-1 divides m² + n² only if it divides both m and n.

§316. Corollary: a sum of two coprime squares has no prime divisor ≡ 3 (mod 4). All its odd prime divisors are ≡ 1 (mod 4). The prime 2 can also divide it, exactly when both squares are odd.

§317. Case -1 a residue: complements of residues are residues, and complements of non-residues are non-residues. Case -1 a non-residue: complements of residues are non-residues, and complements of non-residues are residues.
- The last clause uses non-residue × non-residue = residue. For squares this was presumably established earlier in the chapter (cf. §§320, 322).

§318. If d = 2p+1 with p even, it is so far only shown that -1 *can* be a residue, not that it *must* be. To settle this, Euler proposes to compare the quadratic residues with the residues of a geometric progression of powers mod 2p+1 whose number of distinct residues is exactly p.

§319. Assume a has order p mod 2p+1. The existence of such an a is assumed, not proved. Then:
- the 'residues' are H = {1, a, ..., a^{p-1}};
- the 'non-residues' are the coset A·H = {A, Aa, ..., Aa^{p-1}}, with A ∉ H.

§320. Like quadratic residues, H has three properties:
1) it contains 1;
2) the product of two residues is a residue;
3) residue × non-residue is a non-residue.
Euler announces the consequence: non-residue × non-residue is a residue (H has index 2).

§321 (marginal addition). If 2p+1 | a^p - 1, then a is a quadratic residue.
- Implicit (mine): every quadratic residue α = n² satisfies α^p = n^{2p} ≡ 1 by Fermat.
- If a were a quadratic non-residue, the products aα, aβ, ... would run through all non-residues, and each satisfies (aα)^p ≡ 1.
- Then every x prime to 2p+1 would satisfy x^p ≡ 1, which Euler calls absurd. Modern justification: a polynomial of degree p has at most p roots mod a prime, but there are 2p nonzero classes.
- This is the 'if' half of Euler's criterion.

§322. Heuristic argument for the power residues: if non-residue × non-residue were a non-residue, the non-residues would outnumber the residues, contradicting the equal counts.

§323 (firmer proof, continued on p.40). Fix the non-residue A; any other non-residue is Aa^n. Their product is A²a^n. If this were a non-residue it would be ≡ Aa^m, with m > n after adding multiples of p. Next page: cancelling Aa^n gives A ≡ a^{m-n}, so A ∈ H, a contradiction. Hence non-residue × non-residue is a residue.

Purpose of the whole sequence: identify H with the quadratic residues (§§325-326), giving Euler's criterion and, for p even, that -1 is a quadratic residue (§§330-332). This is the route to proving that every prime 4q+1 divides a sum of two coprime squares.
errors: §315: the passage from 'no square ≡ 4q-1-α' to 'm²+n² never divisible' tacitly needs n ≢ 0 (mod 4q-1) so that nn is a genuine nonzero residue; the exception clause covers this, but the step is not argued.
§316: Euler does not note that 2 can divide a sum of two coprime squares at most once (4 never divides it); this is an omission rather than an error.
§317: the last clause (complements of non-residues are residues when -1 is a non-residue) relies on non-residue × non-residue = residue for quadratic residues, which is not proved on this page.
§319: the existence of an element a of exact order p mod 2p+1 is assumed, not proved (it is equivalent to the existence of primitive roots, which Euler never proved rigorously).
§321: 'quod est absurdum' is unjustified on the page; it needs the fact that x^p ≡ 1 (mod prime) has at most p solutions (Lagrange 1768; Euler had related difference arguments).
§322: the counting argument is heuristic and not a proof; Euler himself replaces it with the firmer argument of §323.

results.what: For a prime 4q-1, -1 is a quadratic non-residue: the complement of every residue is a non-residue
results.modern_name: First supplement to quadratic reciprocity, (-1/p) = -1 for p ≡ 3 mod 4

results.what: A sum of two coprime squares has no prime divisor ≡ 3 (mod 4); its odd prime divisors are ≡ 1 (mod 4), and 2 occurs when both squares are odd
results.modern_name: Prime divisors of x²+y² with gcd(x,y)=1

results.what: Residues of the powers of an element of order p mod 2p+1 form an index-2 subgroup with the same multiplicative rules as quadratic residues (non-residue × non-residue = residue)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (E262, 1761, theorems on power residues); group-theoretic form later (Gauss)

results.what: If 2p+1 divides a^p - 1, then a is a quadratic residue mod 2p+1

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known content of Euler's Tractatus (c.1750, published 1849): quadratic residues, -1 mod 4q-1, prime divisors of sums of two squares, and Euler's criterion via power residues. All of it is standard and already attributed to Euler; the only small details are the marginal §321 and the incomplete rigor.

checkable.sympy: all(not is_quad_residue(-1 % p, p) for p in primerange(3, 2000) if p % 4 == 3)
checkable.asserts: -1 is a quadratic non-residue for every prime p ≡ 3 mod 4 (§314)

checkable.sympy: all((a*a + b*b) % p != 0 for p in [3,7,11,19,23,31,43] for a in range(1, p) for b in range(1, p))
checkable.asserts: No prime 4q-1 divides m²+n² unless it divides both m and n (§315)

checkable.sympy: all(all(f % 4 == 1 or f == 2 for f in factorint(m*m + n*n)) for m in range(1, 60) for n in range(1, 60) if gcd(m, n) == 1)
checkable.asserts: Prime divisors of a sum of two coprime squares are 2 or ≡ 1 mod 4 (§316)

checkable.sympy: all(factorint(m*m + n*n).get(2, 0) <= 1 for m in range(1, 60) for n in range(1, 60) if gcd(m, n) == 1)
checkable.asserts: 2 divides a coprime sum of two squares at most once (supplement to §316)

checkable.sympy: all((pow(a, (P-1)//2, P) == 1) == is_quad_residue(a, P) for P in primerange(3, 300) for a in range(1, P))
checkable.asserts: Euler's criterion: a^p ≡ 1 mod 2p+1 iff a is a quadratic residue (§321, both directions)

checkable.sympy: all(set(pow(a, k, P) for k in range((P-1)//2)) == set(x*x % P for x in range(1, P)) for P in primerange(3, 200) for a in range(2, P) if n_order(a, P) == (P-1)//2)
checkable.asserts: The powers of an element of order p mod 2p+1 are exactly the quadratic residues (§§319, 326)

checkable.sympy: all(is_quad_residue(A*B % P, P) for P in primerange(3, 100) for A in range(1, P) for B in range(1, P) if not is_quad_residue(A, P) and not is_quad_residue(B, P))

Otherwise the transcription agrees with the image; the footnote (*) states that §321 is written in the margin of the autograph.
